# TCP animated episodes

The founder as an animated character, in short comedy episodes that teach one idea, for TikTok. Each
episode follows the master brief (v1.2): entertainment, then the idea, then TCP, then one ask. Every
episode is made twice from one master: once for the TCP account and once for the founder's own.

**How they're made.** The character is drawn in code (`brand/source/reels/toon/`), not generated by
an AI image or video model. He's a detailed 2D cartoon: inked outlines, shading from the screen's
light, and the founder's own proportions, taken from his photos and drawn as a true three-quarter
view. His six-panel cap, his collar and his chains are small 3D models turned to
the same angle as his face, so the brim, seams, eyelets and crown logo sit in true perspective and
the chains drape round his neck and down his chest; the same models give the cap
worn backwards and the view from behind. His hair is cut short under the cap. He's built strong:
a thick neck, round shoulders, a deep chest narrowing to the waist. Each arm is a shoulder, elbow and
wrist placed as it would really be seen from that angle, with the sleeve following the muscle under
it, so his arms keep their length in every pose. His hands are drawn from their bones to real
proportions (tapered fingers, knuckle creases, nails), so they hold the mouse, the keyboard and the
phone properly; in the phone shot his hand holds it as he would see it himself. The brand's name
on his chest wraps round it and stays readable when he faces the other way. His face, cap, clothes
and chains are built from fixed shapes, so they can't drift between shots. Episodes are scripts in `brand/source/reels/specs/`, rendered by the reel
studio like the other reels. Charts in the stories are examples, labelled on screen. App footage is
the real Quant Terminal in demo mode, labelled DEMO PRICES.

**Files for each episode** (1080 × 1920, 30 fps):

| File | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `tcp-<episode>-music.mp4` | The TCP account, with TCP's own music and sound effects |
| `tcp-<episode>-sfx.mp4` | The sound effects only. Add a trending sound in TikTok and keep the original sound at about 50% |
| `tcp-<episode>-personal-music.mp4`, `-personal-sfx.mp4` | The same two, cut for the founder's account |
| `tcp-<episode>-cover.jpg`, `-personal-cover.jpg` | The cover frames |

**The character sheet** (`tcp-founder-character-sheet.png`, V6) is the canonical look for his face
and cap: Lewis approved it on 5 October 2026, and they change only on purpose.

**His wardrobe.** Since 16 October 2026, at Lewis's request, he wears a different designer outfit
and different diamond chains in every episode: crewnecks, hoodies, knits, zip-up track tops, varsity
jackets and puffers, with tennis, Cuban and rope chains in white, yellow or rose gold, some iced,
some with a crown pendant. Each spec names its look with `outfit:` (the looks are `OUTFITS` in
`toon/founder.js`), and no two episodes share one. Brand names appear as plain lettering on the
clothes, never as logos.

## EP02 · Every Trader Has Done This

### A. Episode card

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | Every Trader Has Done This |
| Pillar | Trading comedy, with one lesson |
| Length | 26.6 s |
| Accounts | TCP (`tcp-ep02-every-trader-*`) and personal (`tcp-ep02-every-trader-personal-*`) |
| The idea | Wait for the trap, then the structure, then the pullback |
| Ask | TCP: *Follow TCP*. Personal: *Follow for the next one* |

The brief's ask for this episode was "follow / free community". It's follow only: joining the Inner
Circle needs a broker account through the partner link, so calling it free would mislead, and asking
TikTok viewers to open a CFD account is a regulated promotion in the UK. The link in bio and the bot
handle joining, with the disclosures.

### B. Hook options

Ranked by how different the mechanism is, not by how well they'd do.

1. **"just one more breakout…"** (used). Self-recognition: the viewer hears their own inner voice
   before anything happens, and stays to see it go wrong.
2. **"every trader has done this"** (the TCP cut's line above it). A challenge: viewers want to see
   whether they have, and the comments fill with "not me" and tags.
3. **"POV: you called it a fakeout"**. The POV format puts the viewer in the chair, and "fakeout"
   is a word they'll want explained.

### C. Final timed script

No voice. On-screen text only.

| Time | On screen | Text |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–2.0 | His eyes on the screen, leaning in; then the desk at night | TCP cut: EVERY TRADER HAS DONE THIS (small). Both: *just one more breakout…* |
| 2.0–4.6 | Price breaks the range high. Click. BUY. The next candle slams through his stop | — |
| 4.6–6.0 | He freezes, then looks at the camera. Silence | *fakeout.* |
| 6.0–8.9 | Price falls to the range low. Click. SELL. It sweeps the lows and rips back through his stop | *so I flipped it.* |
| 8.9–10.0 | Disbelief. Silence | *twice.* |
| 10.0–12.0 | He leans back, arms folded | *ok. what actually happened?* |
| 12.0–18.4 | The chart rewinds and replays with gold marks | *1 THE TRAP · both of those trades*, *2 STRUCTURE TURNS · a higher high*, *3 THE PULLBACK · then you get in*, then *trap → structure → pullback* |
| 18.4–19.8 | A small smirk and a nod | — |
| 19.8–23.8 | His phone: the Quant Terminal's Markets tab, the levels drawn on its chart | *traps get set at the levels everyone watches.* then *the Quant Terminal marks them for me.* |
| 23.8–26.6 | End card | TCP / *Follow TCP* / *The Quant Terminal, inside Telegram.* / the risk line |

### E. Character continuity

- **Outfit, every shot:** black cap worn forward with the gold TCP crown, the pearl chain, a black
  crewneck. No shades in this episode.
- **Expressions:** urgent (brows down, lids narrow) at the screen; frozen, then the side-eye to
  camera (shot 6); disbelief (eyes wide, brows up, mouth open) in shot 10; tired and thinking in shot
  11; a small smirk in shot 13. He never grins.
- **Pose:** right hand on the mouse and left hand on the keyboard until shot 11; arms folded from
  shot 11.
- **Props:** monitor, keyboard, mouse, a black mug with the crown, his phone.
- **Continuity:** one pose track and one chart track run under every shot, so a cut never changes
  what he's doing or where the price is.

### F. Environment

- **Where:** his desk at home, at night. A window behind him with the city lit up; a framed TCP print
  on the wall; a warm gold light strip behind the desk.
- **Light:** the monitor is the key light, cool on his face. It turns red when a big red candle
  prints and green on the rip, so the chart's moves land on his face. Warm gold from behind.
- **Colour:** black and warm gold, cool screen light. Red and green only come from the chart.
- **Background action:** none. No other people.

### G. Animation

The tool is the reel studio. `brand/source/reels/specs/ep02-every-trader.js` is the whole episode:
each shot is one line (set, start, end, camera keys), the founder's poses are one list of keys, and
the chart's progress is another. To change a moment, change its line and render again:

```sh
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W --stills=4.3,9.5      # check a moment
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W                        # the TCP cut
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W --variant=personal     # the founder's cut
```

The sets are in `toon/toon.js` (`desk`, `ots`, `screen`, `mouse`) and the character in
`toon/founder.js`. Continuity rules for any change: no new clothes or jewellery, the crown always on
the cap's front, five fingers on every visible hand, and chart text that is real and readable.

### H. Product

- **19.8–23.8:** the real Quant Terminal on his phone, held in his hand: the Markets tab, scrolling
  from the price and the engine briefing to the 15-minute chart with the previous day's high and low
  and the Asia range drawn on. It's footage of the app itself (`capture.cjs`, shot `markets`), in
  demo mode, labelled DEMO PRICES above the phone.
- **The end card** names it: *The Quant Terminal, inside Telegram.*
- Nothing else in the episode is product: the chart on his monitor is a story chart, labelled
  EXAMPLE CHART · NOT REAL PRICES.

### I. Edit map

- **Tempo:** cuts sit on a 120 bpm grid (a beat is 0.5 s): 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.6, 6.0, 7.0, 8.9 (the
  rip's stop-out leads it), 10.0, 12.0, 18.4, 19.8, 23.8.
- **Music** (the `-music` cut): in from the first frame, out at 4.34 and 8.64 for the punchlines,
  back at 6.0 and 10.0. With a trending sound, use the `-sfx` cut and let the sound's own drop land
  near 4.3 if it can.
- **Text:** one thought at a time, popping in on the beat. Lesson notes at 13.9, 15.1 and 16.3, each
  held 1.2 s.
- **Zooms:** slow push-ins on every shot; the stop-outs get a 0.45 s shake and a red edge.
- **Speed:** the replay rewinds 15 candles in 0.5 s, plays the trades back in 1 s, then slows to a
  candle every 0.4 s for the lesson.
- **Effects:** clicks at 3.15 and 7.15; slams at 4.3 and 8.6; whoosh at 12.12; pops at 13.9, 15.1
  and 16.3; a rise at 17.0; a whoosh into the end card.

### J. Personal account version

- **End card:** *Follow for the next one* / *Every trader has done this.*

- **Hook:** *EVERY TRADER HAS DONE THIS* above *just one more breakout…*, with the TCP badge in the

- **Caption:**

```
Be honest: how many times have you? 👇

```

### L. QA

- **Narrative:** the joke works without sound; each beat is one shot; the lesson comes from the
  story (his two losses *are* the trap).
- **Visual:** one drawing of him in every shot; five fingers on every hand; no warped screens; chart
  and app text is real and readable; no floating objects (the phone is in his hand); no neon "AI
  trader" look.
- **Trading:** one idea; no statistics; the chart says it's an example; no profit claims; no luxury
  shots.
- **Product:** the app footage is the real app, labelled demo; what the caption says it does (draw
  the levels) is what it does.
- **Brand:** the crown on his cap, on the wall print and on his mug; gold only as an accent; one ask.
- **Platform:** text clear of TikTok's buttons and caption area (checked with `--safe`); readable at
  phone size; works muted.
- **Labels:** no AI voice and no AI-generated imagery, so TikTok's AI label isn't needed. Add it if
  in doubt; it costs nothing.

### M. Cover

The opening close-up at 0.9 s: his eyes on the screen and *just one more breakout…* (the TCP cut adds
EVERY TRADER HAS DONE THIS above it). If TikTok asks for cover text, use *every trader has done this*.

### N. Caption and hashtags

In J and K. Keep the risk line last.

### O. Production split

- **Made here:** script, character, sets, animation, chart, captions, music and effects, both cuts,
  covers, captions for posting.
- **You:** choose a trending sound if you want one (use the `-sfx` file); post each cut to its
  account at the times in P; tell me what the comments say.

### P. Posting

UK times. The two accounts post a day apart, so the same story never goes out twice in one day.

| When | Account | File | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon 5 Oct, 19:30 | TCP | `tcp-ep02-every-trader-music.mp4` | TikTok, caption K |
| Mon 5 Oct, 20:00 | TCP | the same file | Instagram Reels, caption K |
| Tue 6 Oct, 19:30 | Founder | `tcp-ep02-every-trader-personal-music.mp4` | TikTok, caption J |
| Tue 6 Oct, 20:00 | Founder | the same file | Instagram Reels, caption J |

- **Cover:** the frame at 0.9 s (`-cover.jpg`); if TikTok asks for cover text, *every trader has done
  this*.
- **Pin** it to the founder's profile; on TCP's, it joins the three pins in `POSTS.md` once batch 1 is
  up.
- **No AI label needed:** no AI voice and no AI imagery. With a trending sound, use the `-sfx` file
  and keep the original sound at about 50%.
- **The first hour:** answer the early comments, ideally with a short video reply; TikTok pushes
  replies. Note the three-second hold rate after a day.

## EP08 · The Day I Deleted 27 Indicators

### A. Episode card

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | The Day I Deleted 27 Indicators |
| Pillar | Trading comedy, with one lesson |
| Length | 23.3 s |
| Accounts | TCP (`tcp-ep08-27-indicators-*`) and personal (`tcp-ep08-27-indicators-personal-*`) |
| The idea | 27 opinions bury the price; one clear view, built for how you trade, shows it |
| Ask | TCP: *Follow TCP*. Personal: *Follow for the next one* |

### B. Hook options

1. **"the day I deleted 27 indicators"** (used). The number makes it specific and a little absurd,
   and the buried chart proves it in the first frame.
2. **"I couldn't find the price."** A confession: anyone who's done it stays to see the fix.
3. **"just one more indicator…"** (used as the turn). It runs on from EP02's "just one more
   breakout…", so followers get the callback.

### C. Final timed script

No voice. On-screen text only.

| Time | On screen | Text |

| 0.0–2.0 | His chart, buried under 27 indicators | *the day I deleted 27 indicators* |
| 2.0–3.0 | Him, leaning in, squinting | *I couldn't find the price.* |
| 3.0–6.5 | How it happened: one average, then indicator after indicator, faster and faster, the price squeezed into a strip | *it started with one.* then *just one more indicator…* |
| 6.5–8.0 | All 27: lines, clouds, bands, BUY and SELL tags everywhere, the count at 27 | *every one had an opinion.* |
| 8.0–9.0 | The side-eye to camera. Silence | — |
| 9.0–10.0 | Right-click, *Remove all indicators*, click | — |
| 10.0–11.0 | They drop away, 27 to 0 | — |
| 11.0–12.5 | Just the candles | *oh. there it is.* |
| 12.5–15.0 | His own indicator, TCP QT, comes on: the chart zooms in, then the sessions, the H4 zone, the averages, the fib, the structure tags, the liquidity lines and its dashboard, block by block. The count reads 1 | *now I use one.* then *my own.* (gold) |
| 15.0–16.5 | A small smirk and a nod, his view on the monitor behind him | — |
| 16.5–18.5 | The dashboard up close: trend matrix, regime, setup, order flow | *trend, zones, order flow.* |
| 18.5–20.5 | The whole chart again | *on one chart.* |
| 20.5–23.3 | End card | TCP / *Follow TCP* / *One lesson an episode.* / the risk line, and *Example chart with example values, not real trades.* |

### E. Character continuity

- **Outfit, every shot:** as approved on sheet V6: black cap worn forward with the gold TCP crown, the
  pearl chain, the black AMIRI crewneck. No shades.
- **Expressions:** urgent at the screen; a squint in shot 2; the side-eye to camera in shot 5; a small
  smirk and a nod in shot 10. He never grins.
- **Pose:** right hand on the mouse, left hand on the keyboard, the whole episode.
- **Props:** monitor, keyboard, mouse, the black mug with the crown, his phone.

### F. Environment

- **Where:** his desk at night, as in EP02. The screen shots pull back far enough to show the monitor
  standing on the desk, with the keyboard, mouse and mug out of focus below it.
- **Light:** the monitor is the key light. It turns more violet as the indicators pile up and back to
  cool white when they're gone.

### G. Animation

`brand/source/reels/specs/ep08-27-indicators.js` is the whole episode, on the same pose and chart tracks
as EP02. The chart is EP08's own (`story: 'clutter'` in `toon/toon.js`): 64 example candles with 200
more of history behind them, and 27 indicators each worked out from those candles (averages, bands,
clouds, levels, oscillators), so nothing on it is scribbled. The menu is drawn plainly, with no
platform's branding. The count is the joke, so it's whole in every frame: the camera holds the legend
and the count together up to a scale of 0.62, and any push past that heads for the count.

The ending is Lewis's own indicator, TCP QT v11.7, as it looks on his chart (he made its look public
on 6 October 2026). `tcpView()` in `toon/toon.js` draws it from his screenshot on the same example
candles: the sessions, the H4 zone, the 9, 21 and 50 averages, a fib from the swing low to the swing
high, CHoCH and BOS tags, BSL, SSL and PWL, and the dashboard. Every value on it is an example. How the
indicator works out what it shows, its code and its settings stay out of the repo.

```sh
node render.cjs ep08-27-indicators $W --stills=0.5,9.5,14.95  # check a moment
node render.cjs ep08-27-indicators $W                         # the TCP cut
node render.cjs ep08-27-indicators $W --variant=personal      # the founder's cut
```

### H. Product

- **12.5–20.5:** his own indicator, TCP QT v11.7: its look only, on the example chart, with example
  values. Its dashboard names the market (GOLD 15m) as his does; the prices on it are made up.
- **The end card:** *One lesson an episode.* The risk line adds *Example chart with example values,
  not real trades.*
- The chart on his monitor is a story chart, labelled EXAMPLE CHART · NOT REAL PRICES.

### I. Edit map

- **Tempo:** cuts on the 120 bpm grid: 2.0, 3.0, 6.5, 8.0, 9.0, 9.6, 10.0, 12.5, 15.0, 16.5, 20.5.
- **Music** (the `-music` cut): in from the first frame, out from 8.0 (the side-eye) to 11.0 (*oh.
  there it is.*).
- **The climb:** indicators come on faster and faster (each a little sooner than the last), 26 in

- **The wipe:** 27 to 0 in 0.9 s, the count running down with them.

### L. QA

- **The count is honest:** 27 named indicators, each drawn from the candles, and the legend and panes
  list every one.
- **Narrative:** works without sound; one beat a shot; the lesson comes from the story.
- **Visual:** the approved drawing of him in every shot; five fingers on every hand; chart, menu and
  app text real and readable; no warped screens.
- **Trading:** one idea; no statistics; no profit claims; the chart says it's an example; no indicator
  or platform is named as bad. His indicator shows its look only: no hit rate, no win rate, no
  results, and nothing on how it works out what it shows.
- **Platform and labels:** text clear of TikTok's buttons; no AI voice or AI imagery.

The opening frame at 0.9 s: the buried chart with the count at 27 and *the day I deleted 27
indicators*. If TikTok asks for cover text, use the same line.

Ten episodes for Saturday 17 to Monday 26 October, after EP08 on Friday 16. Each is somewhere
new, with its own music, and three come straight from the master brief (EP06, EP09 and the line-up
that brings in the brief's FOMO character). The founder is in every one, as approved on sheet V6.

**The cast** (`toon/cast.js`; Lewis approved cast sheet V1, `tcp-cast-sheet.png`, on 14 October 2026):
the trading emotions, candlesticks come to life, with rubber-hose arms and legs, white gloves and
trainers. They're made up, drawn in code like him, so they look the same in every shot.

| Who | Look | What it says |

| FOMO | a tall green candle, its wick sparking, can't keep still | *it's pumping!* |
| REVENGE | a red candle in boxing gloves and a headband, its wick smoking | *win it back!* |

PATIENCE is TCP's: gold, the crown, calm. Whenever the founder wins the argument, PATIENCE is the
idea he's standing for, so the brand ends up on the right side of every story without anyone
saying "join".

Same files as the others (`tcp-<episode>-music.mp4`, `-sfx.mp4`, the `-personal-` pair and the
covers). Covers are the frame at 0.9 s; if TikTok asks for cover text, use the hook.

### What works on TikTok and Reels, and how this set uses it

- **The first second decides it.** A strange picture and a line that opens a question: a police
  line-up of 40 cm candles and *every bad trade has a suspect*; a candle popping up behind a coffee
  and *if FOMO was a person*. The text sits in the top third, clear of the buttons, and the first
  frame already shows the joke, so the cover works as a thumbnail too.
- **Characters people come back for.** A recurring cast turns single videos into a series: people
  follow to see what FOMO does next. Each emotion has its own episode now (FOMO EP09, REVENGE EP18,
  GREED EP19, FEAR EP21, PATIENCE EP22: pin them as a playlist); they cross over (the line-up has
  four, EP22 and EP23 have two); PATIENCE always wins. Keep their looks fixed (the sheet) and their lines in
  character.
- **A loop.** EP09 ends where it began (FOMO pops back up: *every. single. time.*), so the second
  watch starts before people notice. Rewatches count towards watch time, which both apps reward.
- **Short, one idea.** 18 to 23 s, one lesson, the lesson in the last third, cuts on the beat about
  every 2 s. Nothing to explain: the picture tells the joke without sound (most people scroll muted).
- **A question people can answer in one word.** *Which one's in your line-up?* *Ever let greed move
  your target?* One-word answers get comments, and comments push the video out. Reply to the best
  ones with a video reply (TikTok) using the same characters: easy follow-ups.
- **Something to send.** Instagram weighs sends heavily: *tag the friend who…* lines and relatable
  moments (FOMO pulling your sleeve) get shared in DMs. Saves come from a clear takeaway (*your
  target was set when you were calm*).
- **Sound.** The `-music` cut has TCP's own track. The `-sfx` cut keeps just the effects so a
  trending sound can go under it at about 50%: trending audio can help reach, and the effects keep
  the timing.
- **Two accounts, two voices.** The TCP account teaches (*One lesson an episode, from TCP*); the
  founder's account confesses (*put my last bad trade in a line-up*). The same file, a different
  caption, a different crowd.
- **Consistency.** One a day at the same times; reply in the first hour; pin a good comment.

### Promoting TCP without breaking the rules

The ask is always *Follow*. Joining the Inner Circle means opening a broker account through the
partner link, and asking TikTok or Instagram viewers to do that is a regulated financial promotion
in the UK, so the reels never say join, VIP, signals or link in bio, and never show profits. The bio
and the bot do the joining, with the disclosures. What the reels can do, and do:

- show TCP's world: the crown on his cap, the backdrop and podium and ring apron in TCP gold, the
  gold PATIENCE with the crown;
- show TCP's habits as the right answer: no setup, no trade; a plan logged before the result
  (EP06's card says so); done for the day after a loss; taking the target;
- show that there's a group behind him (the press asking for setups in EP06) without naming it or
  asking anyone in;
- end on *Follow TCP* and a question.

The captions follow the same rules and end with the risk line.

*CLOSE IT!! CLOSE IT!!* CLOSED +2 PIPS. Then the price runs all the way to the target without it: a
jump scare, TARGET HIT. *…oh.* *Fear closes winners early. The stop was in. Let the plan work.* FEAR
sinks into its seat. *Ever closed a winner too early?* The film shots look over the audience's
shoulders, with his cap and FEAR's drooping wick in silhouette against the screen. The score is a
drone, a heartbeat and a music box; the jump scare is one flash, nowhere near three a second. The
chart is a drawing, not a market.

Why it should travel: *POV: watching your trade* is a format traders already share, and the horror
film gives it a picture nobody has used; *…oh.* is the payoff people rewatch for; the film's title
card is a screenshot; and *closed it at +2* is a confession half the comments will make.

boot: *GOT ONE!!* *The young ones chase every ripple.* In the hide, the founder whispers: *this one
hasn't moved in 4 hours.* Night comes and goes in a time-lapse (*still waiting*), FOMO shivering in
the water with its boot. At dawn the float goes under: *the setup.* PATIENCE puts its tea down and
lands one gold fish: *one trade. Then it goes home*, past FOMO. *Most of trading is waiting. Be
honest: which one are you?* The captions are the narration (no voice, and no impression of any real
presenter); the score is strings, marimba and a flute over the savanna's birds and insects, and the

the time-lapse is something to watch twice; *which one are you?* has a one-word answer (FOMO or

`specs/ep24-coaster.js`. A theme park at sunset, and a rollercoaster whose track is a price chart:

on to the TARGET station, higher than the first peak. *Every trade is a rollercoaster:* PATIENCE (front
seat, with its tea) and FEAR set off up the chain lift; FOMO waits on a platform at the very top and
leaps in (*WAIT FOR MEEE!!*): *FOMO gets on at the top.* The drop: *LET ME OFF!!* At the bottom FEAR
jumps off, and FOMO with it, dizzy by the net: *FEAR gets off at the bottom.* *PATIENCE rides the
plan* to TARGET. The founder at the ride's controls (a sign: RIDE AT YOUR OWN RISK): *FOMO buys the
top. FEAR sells the bottom.* The whole ride from above: *the stop was the net. It never got there.*
*Which seat are you in?*

Why it should travel: buying the top and selling the bottom is the most relatable pain in trading,
and here it's a picture people get in a second (the track is the chart); the safety net shows the
stop without a lecture; three seats make a one-word answer; and RIDE AT YOUR OWN RISK is the risk
warning as a joke.

## The Fast Lane: sports cars and private jets

Six episodes at speed, made on 17 and 18 October 2026 at Lewis's request: the founder in his
supercar and his private jet, each episode one trading lesson told through driving or flying. The
car is drawn to a real one's measurements (the scissor-doored Lamborghini Aventador: 4.78 m long,
1.14 m high, a 2.70 m wheelbase, bigger tyres at the back than the front) and in its design
language, gloss black with gold wheels, red callipers and the TCP crown instead of a maker's badge;
the jet is cream and gold, boarded by a VIP stair truck. Both are cartoon props, drawn for the
metaphor and never shown as what trading paid for.

**What's new in the studio.** `toon/fastlane.js` adds four sets: `street` (the car on a wet street at
night, its door lifting, him inside; it can pull away), `driver` (him at the wheel, seen from the
passenger seat, with the dash display: the speed, a brake light and the sat nav), `road` (the road
through the windscreen, on the left as in the UK, with signs, traffic lights, a speed camera and a car
ahead) and `tarmac` (the jet on the apron at sunrise, a VIP stair truck and a red carpet). The jet's cabin,
window and overhead panel come from EP01. He has a driving pose (`arms: 'wheel'`), and the music has
a new style, `phonk` (drift phonk: a cowbell riff, a distorted 808 and a hard kick, with two riffs).

**Why it should travel.** Cars and jets stop the scroll; the lesson keeps people watching. Each
picture maps one idea onto something everyone already knows: brakes are a stop loss, a red light is
no setup, a missed exit is a missed trade, a flight plan is a trade plan, turbulence is normal price
movement, and a test drive is a demo account. Each ends on a question people can answer in a word.

**Why the wording stays plain.** Luxury next to trading is what UK regulators (the FCA and the ASA)
watch for: posts that suggest trading pays for the lifestyle. So these episodes never show or
mention winnings, every end card says the car or the jet is a cartoon, the descriptions talk only
about discipline, and the hashtags stay on trading (no #supercar, #luxury or #lifestyle).

| Episode | Length | Music | The lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| FL1 · The Brakes | 23.0 s | drift phonk | Your stop loss is your brakes |
| FL2 · Red Light | 23.0 s | trap | No setup is a red light |
| FL3 · Recalculating | 25.3 s | lo-fi | Missed the entry? Don't chase it |
| FL4 · Flight Plan | 21.6 s | lounge | No plan, no take-off |
| FL5 · Turbulence | 20.2 s | harpsichord minuet | Size your trade for the bumps |
| FL6 · Test Drive | 23.0 s | drift phonk | A demo account is your test drive |

**Posting.** One a day, on the TCP account first and the founder's account an hour and a half later,
as in the earlier weeks. If they all go up in one night, schedule them rather than posting them at
once: posts from one account published together compete with each other for reach.
